# Ezra (full-body MRI cancer-screening, shown here co-branded with Function)

URL: https://www.ezra.com/ (captured page: "Function | ezra" partnership landing)

## Type system
- Display: `"Financier Display", Arial, sans-serif` — H1 88px/300, with
  italic used for the key phrase ("Advanced MRI Scans for *early
  detection*"). Same display family as Function Health (shared design
  system/agency), confirming a recognizable "warm serif + terracotta"
  house style across this cluster of DTC health brands.
- Secondary label type: `F37beckett, Tahoma, sans-serif` at 12px — a small
  serif/slab used for eyebrow labels ("FEATURED IN," "SCAN RESULTS").
- Body/UI: `Ftbase, Arial, sans-serif` 14px/400 — plain functional sans for
  body copy, pricing tables, and navigation.

## Color system
- bg: warm cream `#FEF9EF`.
- text: warm near-black `#2A2B2F`.
- surface/card: white `#FFFFFF`.
- accent: terracotta/rust `#B05A36` — CTA buttons ("Book Your Scan"),
  underlines, and pricing-card accents.
- Dark footer band: near-black `#2A2B2F`.

## Layout & grid
- Centred, editorial hero: headline + subhead + single CTA, no photo behind
  the text — text-first rather than image-first.
- A co-branding card ("Function | ezra... have united to give you a more
  complete view inside your body") sits directly below the hero as a
  trust/partnership signal.
- A single large macro photograph (an outstretched hand, dramatically lit)
  fills a full section by itself — spare, gallery-like image use rather
  than lifestyle photography grids.
- Pricing/package section uses a clean 3-up card grid (MRI Scan / MRI Scan
  with Spine / MRI Scan with Skeletal & Neurological Assessment) each
  listing included body regions with checkmarks, followed by a separate
  CT Scans row.

## Sections (order observed)
1. Text-first hero: "Advanced MRI Scans for early detection" + subhead +
   CTA
2. Function×Ezra partnership card
3. Full-bleed dramatic macro photo (hand)
4. Press logo row (Washington Post, Fast Company, NYT, The Economist, New
   Yorker) + Forbes/NBC badges
5. "Ezra has helped 6% of our members identify potential cancer" — stat
   callout with a "Scan Results" UI preview graphic (abstract circular scan
   imagery)
6. "Early cancer detection has an 80% survival rate, compared to less than
   20% for late-stage cancer" — large stat statement, no chart, just bold
   typography
7. "Our scan is designed to detect potential cancer" — 3-step process
   (Book your scan / Get your MRI Scan / View your results)
8. Pricing/package grid: MRI Scan (£1,299), MRI Scan with Spine (£1,999),
   MRI Scan with Skeletal & Neurological Assessment (£5,495), plus Lung CT
   Scan (£399) — each with time estimate and included-regions checklist
9. Dark testimonial band: "To know is to thrive" + patient quote
   ("My doctors told me that had I not gotten that scan, it could have
   easily been 5 to 10 years before the tumor had been discovered")
10. Dark footer with partnership/contact links

## Components/signature
- Pricing transparency at line-item level (exact GBP prices, exact scan
  duration in minutes, exact included body regions with checkmarks) is
  the most detailed, retail-like pricing presentation in the dataset —
  most competitors hide pricing behind a membership paywall or "starting
  at" language.
- Large statistic stated in prose/typography only ("80% vs <20% survival")
  rather than as a chart — relies on the number itself being dramatic
  enough.

## Motion/interactions
- Minimal; the "Scan Results" section includes what appears to be an
  abstract circular imaging-preview graphic, likely with subtle
  rotation/glow rather than literal interactive charting.

## Biomarker/trust presentation
- No biomarker table; instead uses a single dramatic mortality-statistic
  (80% vs 20% survival) as the core trust/urgency device, reinforced by a
  first-person patient testimonial with a specific, emotionally loaded
  outcome (tumor caught early).
- Press logos from major outlets (Washington Post, NYT, Economist, New
  Yorker) plus Forbes/NBC badges anchor credibility; no visible clinician
  credential grid on this page (the co-branding with Function stands in
  for institutional trust).
- Itemized pricing with exact scan duration and included body regions
  functions as its own trust device — transparency as credibility.

## What works
- Detailed, line-item pricing (exact currency amounts, exact minutes,
  exact body-region checklist) removes ambiguity that most competitors in
  this category leave vague — directly reusable as a conversion pattern
  for any diagnostic/scan product.
- A single large, dramatic statistic stated as bold typography (not a
  chart) can be more emotionally effective than a data visualization for a
  mortality/urgency claim.

## Avoid
- Sharing an identical type system (Financier Display + terracotta) with
  Function Health in this dataset means this specific palette/font
  combination is already becoming a recognizable "DTC health-tech serif"
  cliché — vary the accent hue or serif choice if the goal is
  differentiation within the category.
- Extremely light (300) serif at 88px needs a plain, sturdy sans nearby for
  contrast — don't run two light-weight faces together.

## How to apply
- Present diagnostic/scan pricing as an itemized, transparent grid (price,
  duration, included regions/checklist) rather than a vague "starting at"
  membership tier, especially for one-time-purchase scan products.
- Pair one dramatic, plainly-stated statistic with a real patient
  testimonial to carry urgency/trust, instead of defaulting to a chart.
